body:
## Pull request overview

This PR upgrades all `@objectstack/*` core dependencies to `0.8.0` (bringing in Zod v4-based validation) across the monorepo, removes now-unnecessary core patches, and tightens test setup and field widget prop handling.

**Changes:**
- Bumped all direct usages of `@objectstack/{cli,core,driver-memory,objectql,plugin-msw,runtime,client,spec}` from `0.7.2` to `0.8.0` in root, apps, packages, and examples, and updated the lockfile (including Zod dependency wiring inside objectstack packages).
- Removed legacy `@objectstack/core` patch machinery (patch files, `patchedDependencies` in `package.json`, and corresponding lockfile entries) now that upstream APIs are aligned.
- Unified Vitest setup for plugins and the console app, and refined field widgets to spread through additional props while adjusting how `className` is handled.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 37 out of 38 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

By adding `{...props}` to the `Input` here, any internal props passed by the schema renderer (e.g. `schema`, other metadata) will now be forwarded down to the underlying DOM `<input>`, which can produce React warnings about unknown DOM attributes and makes the field API easier to misuse. Since the schema metadata is already consumed via `field || (props as any).schema`, consider explicitly omitting non-DOM props before spreading (or only forwarding a whitelist like `className`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) to keep the rendered HTML clean.

Similar to `UrlField`, introducing `{...props}` on this `Input` means schema-level props like `schema` (see `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`) will now be forwarded to the DOM `<input>`, which can cause invalid/unknown attribute warnings and leak internal metadata into the HTML. It would be safer to destructure and drop non-DOM props before spreading, or explicitly forward only DOM-safe props (e.g. `className`, `id`, `data-*`, `aria-*`).
